input: How will optimizing multi-stop storm restoration routes improve customer SAIDI minutes during the active gale?
expected_output:
### Executive Summary
**Optimizing multi-stop storm restoration routes reduces overall travel latency and sequences fault isolations by customer density and upstream feeder topology, yielding an estimated 38.2% reduction in SAIDI minute accumulation across affected operating zones. Under active gale conditions, clustering proximate trouble tickets (e.g., downed lateral lines and blown transformer fuses along shared corridors) mitigates cumulative customer-hours of interruption compared to traditional first-in, first-out (FIFO) dispatch. Implementing route optimization ensures high-yield switching and restoration tasks are resolved first, significantly shortening the tail of the outage duration curve.**

---

### Data Presentation

| Metric | Current Value | Baseline / Target | Delta (%) | Status (Normal/Warning/Critical) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Storm Mode SAIDI Contribution** | 47.4 min | 76.7 min (Unoptimized FIFO) | -38.2% | **Warning** |
| **Mean Time to Dispatch & Transit (MTTD/T)** | 24.6 min | 41.2 min | -40.3% | **Warning** |
| **Restoration Velocity (Customers/Crew-Hr)** | 18.4 cust/hr | 11.2 cust/hr | +64.3% | **Normal** |
| **ETR Accuracy Deviation ($\Delta$ ETR)** | $\pm$14.2 min | $\pm$38.5 min | -63.1% | **Normal** |
| **Active Gale Hazard Route Clearance** | 91.8% safe routing | 100.0% safe routing | -8.2% | **Critical** |

*Note: Baseline reflects standard static dispatching under equivalent active gale storm conditions (sustained winds 39–54 mph). Metric definitions strictly adhere to IEEE 1366 reliability calculation standards.*

---

### Visualization Triggers
- **Recommended Chart**: Multi-Series Grouped Bar Chart comparing Baseline FIFO SAIDI impact vs. Multi-Stop Route Optimization impact grouped by high-outage feeder zones.
- **Visualizer Configuration**:

```json
{
  "chart_type": "bar",
  "title": "Storm SAIDI Impact: Standard Dispatch vs. Multi-Stop Routing",
  "data": {
    "labels": [
      "Zone North - Feeder 12",
      "Zone North - Feeder 14",
      "Zone Central - Feeder 08",
      "Zone East - Feeder 22",
      "Zone South - Feeder 05"

    "datasets": [
      {
        "label": "Standard FIFO Dispatch SAIDI (min)",
        "data": [142, 118, 95, 84, 62]
      },
      {
        "label": "Optimized Multi-Stop Route SAIDI (min)",
        "data": [88, 71, 54, 49, 38]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

---

### Actionable Recommendations
1. **Prioritize Mainline & Backbone Isolation**: Route initial crews to 3-phase trunk line disconnects and switchgear prior to handling single-phase lateral taps to restore maximum downstream customer blocks immediately.
2. **Cluster Multi-Stop Dispatches by Roadway Passability**: Integrate real-time wind-hazard and roadway obstruction telemetry into GIS routing to eliminate deadheaded transit runs.
3. **Stage Staging Site Replenishment**: Pre-position mobile materials trucks at designated substation staging zones to support rapid multi-stop restock cycles without returning to central service centers.

---

```yaml
tier_2_operation:
  operation_type: "CREW_DISPATCH_REROUTE"
  trigger_reason: "Dynamic multi-stop route optimization approval during Active Gale Emergency Mode"
  target_assets:

      assigned_feeder: "Feeder 12 (Substation North)"
      route_sequence: ["TICKET-8821 (Feeder Trunk)", "TICKET-8834 (Lateral Tap)", "TICKET-8849 (Fused Cutout)"]

```
